item.text:
**7B.7 Research Note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is strongly negative. Egypt under Sisi used legal, security, and media controls to suppress scrutiny, punish journalists and activists, and keep corruption-related reporting away from independent accountability channels. The only positives I found are limited and administrative: some Case 173 relief, a narrow set of complaint investigations, and the existence of an anti-corruption body on paper. None of that shows genuine tolerance for independent accountability of the presidency.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-29 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions | Egyptian authorities detained and prosecuted critics, including journalists and a researcher, using incommunicado detention, abusive pretrial detention, and terrorism-style charges. One case stemmed from reporting on a corruption investigation involving senior pro-Sisi party members, which is direct evidence of punishing investigators and shielding associates. | 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.4 |
| World Report 2024: Egypt | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt | HRW says prosecutors referred three Mada Masr journalists to trial over reporting tied to an unannounced corruption investigation involving senior party members. It also notes asset freezes and travel bans against activists, showing the state kept using judicial power to suppress scrutiny. | 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.4 |
| Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says censorship laws, blocked websites, and media controls remained extensive; it also notes the Supreme Administrative Court upheld the rejection of Mada Masr’s licensing request. This supports a pattern of using state power to neutralize independent media and conceal official conduct. | 7B.7, 7B.6 |
| Egypt: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-net/2024 | The state continued blocking independent news and human-rights sites, with 562 blocked websites by June 2024, including about 132 news links. The report also says the regime could block content without judicial approval and that parliamentary deliberations were not broadcast or published, which is strong concealment evidence. | 7B.7, 7B.6 |
| USDOS – 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Egypt | U.S. Department of State | 2025, covering 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128475.html | The report says the SCMR was president-appointed, had broad discretion to block content, and that the government blocked hundreds of websites and did not publish House and Senate deliberations. It also notes that official media broadly supported state policy. This is strong evidence of institutionalized information control. | 7B.7, 7B.6 |
| Egypt: Lift travel bans imposed on two human rights lawyers | Amnesty International | 2024-07-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-lift-travel-bans-imposed-on-two-human-rights-lawyers/ | Amnesty says Case 173 was closed in March 2024 after 13 years, with travel bans lifted for 29 of 31 NGO workers, but some bans and asset freezes remained. This is a limited positive signal, but it also shows the regime had used years of judicial harassment and financial restrictions to constrain scrutiny. | 7B.7, 7B.6 |
| Major General Amr Adel Named Chairman of the Administrative Control Authority | Administrative Control Authority | 2024 | https://aca.gov.eg/News/3143.aspx | Sisi appointed the ACA chairman, and the ACA presents itself as an oversight body that monitors public bodies and anti-corruption efforts. This is only a weak positive because the body’s leadership is presidentially appointed and the public record does not show it independently scrutinizing Sisi or his inner circle. | 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.4 |

Search gap:
- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of Sisi permitting an independent probe into his own assets, campaign finance, or concealed presidential decisions.
- I also did **not** find evidence that courts, prosecutors, auditors, or media were meaningfully free to pursue senior-regime corruption without retaliation.
- The limited positives are administrative or formal, not proof of genuine accountability.
